solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fellow attracting gossip in part of South America

parts.note: a guy is a fellow, a man
ana is a collection of anecdotes or table talk about someone, hence gossip

explanation.surface: A man draws rumours while travelling in a South American region.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA, a collection of anecdotes about a person, is a crossword stand-by for gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Guyana is a country on the northern coast of the South American continent.

clue.text: More than Happy Hour — epic, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the two words could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A happy hour that turns into an epic session leaves drinkers more than merely cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges HOUR and EPIC together.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated is a step beyond merely happy, so the adjective fits a feeling greater than contentment.

clue.text: Sewers, say, an island put in place

indicators.note: put in tells us the two short pieces go inside the word for place

parts.note: a station is a place or post, as in a person's station

explanation.surface: Someone describes sewage works being installed on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' means drains, not people stitching; 'say' marks them as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Drains and sewage pipes are an example of public hygiene works, the system of keeping a place clean.

clue.text: Chess player with predicament that admits of no escape

parts.note: the two sides in chess are White and Black, so one player is Black
to be in a hole is to be in a predicament

explanation.surface: A chess player finds themselves in a position with no way out.
explanation.definitionFit: Nothing, not even light, can get out of this collapsed region of space, so it admits of no escape.

clue.text: Heads for some water in Margate — for this?

definitions.text: Heads for some water in Margate — for this?

indicators.note: heads means the first letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers head for the sea at Margate, presumably to do this.
explanation.walkthrough: MARGATE is an English seaside resort in Kent. The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down to the sea at a resort suggests a dip, which is what the whole clue describes.

clue.text: One's used to batter, well-chewed food and jelly

parts.note: cud is the food a cow chews over and over
a gel is a jelly-like substance

explanation.surface: A cook lists a batter, well-chewed food and jelly, like a strange recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' looks like cooking but is the verb to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A short thick club is a weapon one uses to beat someone.

clue.text: Picked up blemishes — a lot, but not all — in hypothetical concept

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means the word is lifted, read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: warts are skin blemishes

indicators.note: but not all says the word for a lot loses its last letter

parts.note: many means a lot

explanation.surface: Someone picked up many blemishes, apparently in a purely theoretical idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reverses WARTS to STRAW; 'but not all' cuts MANY to MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a weak, imagined version of an opponent's argument set up only to be knocked down.

clue.text: Very good thing rejected? Greek character returned wail

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lulu is a remarkable or outstanding thing

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so this Greek letter is reversed too

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A fine thing turned down, and a Greek figure sent back with a cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns LULU into ULUL and 'returned' turns ETA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To howl or cry out in a long high trembling voice is to wail.

clue.text: Achievement's to put out fine food

indicators.note: to put out means to expel, so the letter for fine is removed

parts.note: a feat is an achievement; feat's gives the letters with S
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: Someone's achievement is putting out excellent food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like an adjective for the food, but is F.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food or a meal.

clue.text: Note getting out of linen clothing will lead to legal action

indicators.note: getting out of means the note leaves the words for linen clothing

parts.note: lawn is a fine linen fabric
a suit is a set of clothing

explanation.surface: A note found in linen clothes will lead to someone being sued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting out of' removes N from LAWNSUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A case brought before a court is a legal action.

clue.text: The chap is collared by old Greek against religion

indicators.note: collared by means held round the neck, so the old Greek word wraps the others

parts.note: Attic is the dialect and adjective of ancient Athens
he refers to the chap

explanation.surface: A man is seized by an ancient Greek for opposing religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collared by' is the container signal: the old Greek, an Athenian, wraps round the chap and 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Denying the existence of God puts one opposed to religion.

clue.text: Money advanced to hold shareholders' gathering is factor in outburst

indicators.note: to hold means the pair of letters wraps round the meeting

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
an AGM, annual general meeting, is where shareholders gather

explanation.surface: Money lent to stage a shareholders' meeting is behind an angry outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outburst' sounds like temper at the meeting but means a volcanic eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock is the material behind a volcanic eruption.

clue.text: Expatriates filling halls? On the contrary

indicators.note: filling would put the expatriates inside halls, but the clue reverses that
on the contrary flips the filling, so the halls sit inside the word expatriates

explanation.surface: Expatriates are crowding into halls, or perhaps it is the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' then 'On the contrary' says the halls fill Expatriates, so the word is inside ExpATRIAtes.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrium is a central hall in a building, and these are more than one of them.

clue.text: Thug cut in, suppressing loud struggling

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down, so the shortened word keeps the jumbled one inside
cut means shortened, losing its last letter

parts.note: home means in, as in staying in

indicators.note: struggling says the letters of loud are thrashed about

explanation.surface: A thug cuts into a conversation, silencing a loud struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link word here: it means at home, and 'cut' docks its last letter. 'struggling' scrambles loud, and 'suppressing' holds that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodlum is a violent criminal or gangster, so it means a thug.

clue.text: Working daughter about to secure reputation, setting up solo enterprise

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on

indicators.note: in a down clue setting up means raising, reading the letters upward

parts.note: to nab is to secure or seize
a name is a reputation, as in making a name

explanation.surface: A working daughter is about to make a name by starting a solo business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up' reverses D NAB NAME to EMANBAND; 'about to' is link phrasing.
explanation.definitionFit: A business run by a single person who does everything is a solo enterprise.

clue.text: Soldier, when engaged in writing, is a dreamer

indicators.note: engaged in means involved within, so the pieces go inside the writing

parts.note: fist is informal for handwriting
a soldier ant is a kind of ant
as means when

explanation.surface: A soldier who keeps writing letters home is daydreaming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writing' means handwriting, for which fist is old slang; 'engaged in' puts the soldier and 'when' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who indulges in fantasies is a daydreamer.

clue.text: Formerly popular, a low, low note you'll find rarely

parts.note: once means formerly
in means popular, fashionable
blue means low, sad
a low is a cow's moo

explanation.surface: Once a hit, a deep bass note is something you seldom hear now.
explanation.walkthrough: The two lows differ: one is feeling down (BLUE), the other the sound a cow makes (MOO).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very seldom, just as rarely does.

clue.text: Male participating in bid, not entirely out of public view

indicators.note: participating in means taking part within, so the male goes inside
not entirely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an offer is a bid
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A man is involved in a bid that is not fully public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' docks the bid's last letter, and 'participating in' sets the male deer inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of sight of the audience, as backstage, means out of public view.

clue.text: Perhaps last year's weather upset you before, as one averse to change

parts.note: old fog, perhaps, would be last year's weather

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned up, reversed

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A grumble about old weather and an upset person who dislikes change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you before' means you as it was once said, the archaic form; 'upset' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned conservative person resists anything new.

clue.text: Broadband offering Irish rock?

definitions.meaning: a speedy internet connection is a quick net
the ... Rock is a rocky islet off the south coast of Ireland

explanation.walkthrough: The FASTNET Rock, with its lighthouse, gives its name to a famous yacht race.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid internet service is what broadband sells, and an Irish islet bears the same name.

clue.text: Singular exclamations, mostly about book writer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened cries go round the book
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: cries are exclamations

explanation.surface: Singular cries around a book from a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts CRIES to CRIE, which goes 'about' B.
explanation.definitionFit: A copyist or clerk who writes things out by hand is a writer.

clue.text: Notice put on computer peripheral?

parts.note: an ad is a notice
to don is to put on clothes

explanation.surface: An advertisement placed on a computer accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra device attached to a computer is an accessory, and the question mark flags it as one example.

clue.text: Food that is a source of discomfort! One keeps away

parts.note: nosh is informal for food
ow is the cry that pain or discomfort draws

explanation.surface: Food that upsets the stomach makes someone stay away.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark points to OW, the cry of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who fails to turn up stays away from the event.

clue.text: Leave office, completely losing base

indicators.note: losing means the word gives up the letter for base

parts.note: quite means completely
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Someone resigns, abandoning their base entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' is e, the mathematical base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign a job, stepping down from a post, means to leave office.

clue.text: Plan to lose all but end of the argument

indicators.note: all but end of means the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: a row is an argument

explanation.surface: Someone plans to give up all of the argument except its end.
explanation.walkthrough: To THROW a game is to lose it deliberately, hence a planned loss.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberately lose a match is to plan the defeat in advance.

clue.text: Women informed parliamentary official

parts.note: hip means informed, in the know

explanation.surface: Women told an official in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament a party member who enforces discipline and attendance is the WHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A party official who keeps members in line in Parliament has this title.

clue.text: Left in total black, wake up incompletely, continuing to doze

indicators.note: in says the letter for left goes inside the word for total

parts.note: a sum is a total
B is short for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: incompletely means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to rouse is to wake up

explanation.surface: Left in total darkness, someone half wakes and keeps drowsing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the letter for left inside the total, and 'incompletely' docks the last letter of the word for wake up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy or drowsy describes someone still dozing.

clue.text: Operating problem recalled — ditches gadget

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a bug is a problem in an operating system
to bin is to ditch, throw away

explanation.surface: A faulty item is recalled and the manufacturer dumps the device.
explanation.walkthrough: GUBBINS is British slang for a gadget or bits and pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A thingummy or small device is a gadget in informal British speech.

clue.text: Closed, having kept theatre's sponsor cross

indicators.note: having kept means holding inside, so the sponsor sits within

parts.note: to means closed, as a door pushed to
an angel is a financial backer of a theatre production

explanation.surface: A theatre closed, having kept its sponsor, who is angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry, but is a hybrid: this fruit is tangerine crossed with pomelo or grapefruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine-grapefruit hybrid fruit is a cross between two citrus types.
